A.C.M.M, (Mayo Hall) At Bengaluru.

This Petition, Coming On For Reporting
Settlement
, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
ORDER Petitioner who is sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 498A IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, is before this Court.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, the petitioner- accused is the husband of the defacto-complainant and he subjected her to cruelty both mentally and physically and also a demand was made to bring money from her parental home.
3. The respondent No.2 though served with notice has not chosen to appear in person or through her counsel.

4. The petitioner-accused had filed a petition in M.C.No.4611/2020 under Section 13 (1) (a) and (b)
of the Hindu Marriage Act, for dissolving his marriage with the defacto-complainant.
In the said proceedings, the matter was referred to Mediation Center to explore the possibility of amicable settlement between the parties.

The parties before the Mediation Center amicably settled the disputes among themselves, and as per the terms of the settlement, the NC: 2023:KHC:28808 marriage of the accused with the defacto-complainant has been dissolved mutually and permanent alimony of Rs.6 Lakhs is paid to the defacto complainant-respondent No.2 and she has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings.
5. The parties are present before this Court with their respective counsels.

6. Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non-compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably settled their disputes among themselves, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioner is subjected to trial, since the probability of conviction is remote and bleak.
